deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It is an archival cover sheet or label, written in a later hand that is apparently not Riemann's own. It reads: 'Abschrift des Briefes von Riemann an Gauss vom 12. Juni 1850, gefunden in von Ende: Geographische Ortsbestimmungen. Celle 1801 Seite 63.' In English: 'Copy of the letter from Riemann to Gauss of 12 June 1850, found in von Ende: Geographical position determinations, Celle 1801, page 63.' It records the provenance of a copy of a letter from Riemann to Gauss. The copy was found tucked into page 63 of F. A. von Ende's 1801 book on geographic position determinations, plausibly a volume from Gauss's library. In June 1850 Riemann was a student in Göttingen, attending Weber's physics seminar and preparing his doctorate under Gauss. The letter itself is presumably on the following folio(s), which the next-page transcription does not render. The facing page reading 'Herrn Professor Riemann, Hannover[?]' looks like an address leaf or envelope belonging to a different item in the bundle. There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Archival note documenting a copy of a letter from Riemann to Gauss dated 12 June 1850, found in von Ende's 'Geographische Ortsbestimmungen' (Celle 1801), p. 63

deep.surprise_reason: There is no mathematical content. Documented correspondence from the student Riemann to Gauss is scarce, so the provenance note is of minor archival interest. Its significance depends entirely on the contents of the letter itself, which are not on this page.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially correct: 'Abschrift des Briefes / von Riemann an Gauss / vom 12. Juni 1850 / gefunden in / von Ende: Geographische Ortsbestimmungen. Celle 1801 Seite. 63.'
'84' is the archival folio number, written in pencil at the upper right, not part of the text.
The author referred to is presumably Ferdinand Adolph von Ende, a Hanoverian amateur astronomer, author of 'Geographische Ortsbestimmungen' (Celle 1801).
The hand appears to be a later archivist's or editor's, not Riemann's own script.
